articles.title: Michael Irvin rebukes Dak Prescott for an inappropriate comment: “He completely crossed the line”
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys legend was unimpressed by the veteran quarterback’s criticism of the home crowd in Arlington
articles.summary: The Cowboys legend was unimpressed by the veteran quarterback’s criticism of the home crowd in Arlington
articles.body:
M ichael Irvin has taken aim at Dak Prescott after the Dallas Cowboys quarterback criticized the atmosphere at AT&T Stadium following another disappointing defeat as the former wide receiver believes the player directed his frustration towards the wrong people after Sunday's loss to the San Francisco 49ers .

Dallas fell 46-40 in a game that exposed the team's defensive problems once again as San Francisco piled up 584 yards of offense, including 340 in the second half alone, whilst scoring 29 points after the interval to leave the Cowboys with another damaging result.

The defeat featured several embarrassing moments for the Dallas defense, including rookie Kaelon Black running through Caleb Downs and Cobie Durant on a 25-yard touchdown, whilst Deebo Samuel also broke free for a 70-yard score as Brock Purdy even contributing to blocks during the play.

Prescott , meanwhile, threw five touchdown passes and helped Dallas fight back from a 19-point deficit in a great performance from his side of things - however, when asked about having to use a silent count inside his own stadium, he turned his attention to the number of visiting supporters.

“[I] told myself early on that the red was for my high school,” Prescott said post-game. “All I asked for is a great environment to play this game. And unfortunately, their fans were more present than ours.”

Those comments became a talking point on ESPN 's First Take on Monday, where Irvin delivered a blunt assessment as the three-time Super Bowl champion argued that Prescott should not have criticized the supporters, particularly when his remarks could be interpreted as speaking for the entire Cowboys fanbase.

“I certainly thought that he went in a direction that he should not have gone in his press conference,” Irvin said. “Talking about the number of people that were in the stadium, and that he was disappointed that the 49ers fans outstood the Cowboys fans.

“Like, you shouldn't be bewildered by that. You should not be baffled by that. He was speaking for a whole fanbase, and so when Dak gets on the podium and starts talking about the fans, I thought Dak Prescott was totally out of line.”

Defensive woes grow as Jones faces resignation calls

Irvin 's criticism came after a performance that intensified scrutiny of Dallas ' defense as the 49ers averaged an impressive 9.4 yards per play, rushed for 214 yards at 7.4 yards per carry and recorded the most offensive yardage ever conceded by the Cowboys in a home game.

Despite Prescott 's five touchdown passes as George Pickens caught three TD passes and finished with 145 receiving yards as Dallas narrowed the deficit to six points the defense could not prevent San Francisco from controlling the contest and Christian McCaffrey 's 66-yard touchdown reception ended the comeback.

The result left the Cowboys at 4-6, with their hopes of salvaging the season increasingly dependent on improvements across the team as Dallas still remains within reach of the NFC East leaders. However, the latest defensive collapse offered little reassurance that a turnaround is coming.

And pressure is also building around owner and general manager Jerry Jones as former NFL offensive lineman Richie Incognito had questioned his control of football operations before the 49ers game, arguing that Dallas needed an experienced general manager to oversee its roster decisions.

Dallas invested heavily in its personnel, bringing in Rashan Gary , Jalen Thompson , Durant , Dee Winters and Joey Porter Jr. , while selecting Downs and Malachi Lawrence . Yet the additions have not prevented opponents from repeatedly finding space against a defense that remains a major concern.

articles.title: Colin Cowherd tells Jerry Jones why his plan for the Cowboys is going to fall apart
articles.standfirst: Jerry Jones faces growing pressure as Cowboys' locker room problems come under scrutiny
articles.summary: Jerry Jones faces growing pressure as Cowboys' locker room problems come under scrutiny
articles.body:
Colin Cowherd has delivered a blunt assessment of the Dallas Cowboys , and his warning to owner and general manager Jerry Jones goes beyond another disappointing result.

In the broadcaster’s view, it’s a team-wide failure of discipline that raises a much bigger question: do the players genuinely respect head coach Brian Schottenheimer ?

Dallas’ 46-40 home defeat to the San Francisco 49ers provided plenty of evidence for critics. San Francisco piled up an incredible 584 yards of offense, repeatedly finding ways through a defense that has struggled to contain opponents throughout the season.

Three touchdowns came on explosive plays of 74, 70 and 66 yards, making it another miserable afternoon for Dallas supporters at AT&T Stadium.

Cowherd believes the problems extend beyond defensive performances. He pointed to two recent disciplinary incidents involving DeMarvion Overshown and George Pickens . Overshown was penalized after running onto the field during the previous week's game, while Pickens received a taunting penalty against San Francisco.

According to Cowherd , these mistakes suggest players aren't worried about facing meaningful consequences from Schottenheimer .

“Cowboy players don't respect Brian Schottenheimer. They don't care. I mean, you can see it from the penalties, you can see it from the taunting, running on the field. And I mean, I'm just watching,” said Cowherd .

Jerry Jones could be approaching another major coaching decision

The statistics make the situation increasingly difficult to ignore. Through 10 games, Dallas ranked last in total defense, rushing defense and third-down defense, while sitting near the bottom of the league in scoring defense.

"They're on pace for their third straight losing season, and it's got very much a Dave Campo feel to it, where they don't do anything particularly well,” added Cowherd .

“Last in total defense, last in rush defense, last in third-down defense, next-to-last in scoring defense.”

That historical comparison could be particularly interesting for Jones . Campo's Cowboys went 5-11 in three consecutive seasons between 2000 and 2002. Eventually, the disastrous results prompted Jones to make a significant coaching appointment by bringing in Bill Parcells.

Although Parcells didn't deliver a Super Bowl championship, his arrival helped rebuild the roster and restored competitiveness.

Meanwhile, the Cowboys' current defensive struggles have raised questions about coordinator Christian Parker's future. Jones recently acknowledged that the organization is discussing potential changes to Parker's responsibilities following the embarrassing performance against San Francisco.

Schottenheimer has also confirmed that the coaching staff is reviewing the team's performances before deciding what adjustments might be necessary. Jones admitted that evaluating the defensive problems requires considering both coaching decisions and player performances.

However, changing Parker's responsibilities won't necessarily solve Cowherd's biggest concern. A defensive scheme can be adjusted, and coaches can be replaced, but neither decision automatically creates discipline or accountability inside the locker room.

Jones has previously defended the growing pains associated with hiring a young defensive coordinator and making significant personnel changes. Nevertheless, the Cowboys' latest setback puts additional pressure on the entire coaching structure.

articles.title: Jerry Jones is fed up with Cowboys and leaves door open for major coaching change
articles.standfirst: The Dallas Cowboys owner has seen his team's season go up in flames after yet another defensive disasterclass.
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys owner has seen his team's season go up in flames after yet another defensive disasterclass.
articles.body:
The only reason Jerry Jones is still holding out hope for the Dallas Cowboys to make the playoffs is simply because the NFC East is having a down year. Even the first place New York Giants have shown a lot of flaws, even though they're ahead of the 4-6 Cowboys by a few games.

In any other year, the Cowboys would be considered fully dead right now. The past three weeks have featured a meltdown loss against the Arizona Cardinals , a four-point win against a decimated Indianapolis Colts team, and a 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers at home. That latest loss appears to be enough for changes to finally be made.

The Cowboys' defense has been the worst unit in the entire NFL this season, even though the front office focused almost all of their offseason moves on improving that side of the ball. Aside from the new players that were brought in, Jones and co. also fired defensive coordinator Matt Eberflus and brought in rising young defensive coach Christian Parker from the Philadelphia Eagles .

Dallas Cowboys look ready to strip Christian Parker of playcalling duties

The 34-year-old Parker had never called plays before, so growing pains were expected. But Dallas' defense has seemingly regressed despite being historically bad last season . It sounds like Jones has had enough, as he finally admitted this week during his weekly local radio hit that head coach Brian Schottenheimer might have to take away Parker's playcalling duties .

" We are talking about that, but I'm not going to talk about it here. But we are talking about those things. "

Schottenheimer also refused to give Parker a vote of confidence after the loss to the Niners. It's becoming increasingly likely that someone other than Parker will be calling plays for the defense in Week 11 against the Tennessee Titans .

articles.title: Is a shakeup on the horizon for the Cowboys? Jerry Jones refuses to rule out changes involving defensive coordinator Christian Parker
articles.standfirst: Christian Parker's future in Dallas comes under question as Jerry Jones considers changes
articles.summary: Christian Parker's future in Dallas comes under question as Jerry Jones considers changes
articles.body:
Jerry Jones hasn’t announced a coaching shakeup in Dallas , but his latest comments suggest defensive coordinator Christian Parker’s responsibilities could be under review.

Following the Cowboys’ disappointing 46-40 defeat to the San Francisco 49ers, the team owner acknowledged that discussions about possible adjustments are taking place, putting the first-year coordinator under increasing scrutiny.

Speaking Tuesday on 105.3 The Fan, Jones was asked whether Parker’s role or responsibilities could change.

“We’re talking about (making a change), but I’m not going to talk about that here, but we are talking about those things,” said Jones .

He added that any decision could influence preparations for the upcoming matchup against the Tennessee Titans, while also considering what would benefit the team for the remainder of the season. However, no official coaching change has been announced.

Interestingly, Jones hasn't completely lost faith in Parker . He highlighted the 34-year-old’s communication skills, ability to connect with players and potential as a defensive play-caller.

Jones also acknowledged that this is Parker’s first season coordinating an NFL defense, suggesting the young coach could still develop into an effective leader.

In order to reinforce his point, Jones brought up Sean Payton , who temporarily lost offensive play-calling responsibilities during his time with the New York Giants before eventually receiving another opportunity with Dallas.

This suggests that changing Parker’s duties wouldn't necessarily mean the end of his coaching career with the Cowboys.

San Francisco loss intensifies pressure on Dallas

The statistics explain why Dallas is considering adjustments. San Francisco gained 584 total yards at AT&T Stadium, the most ever by a visiting team at the venue, while putting 46 points on the scoreboard. This happened despite Dak Prescott delivering five touchdown passes for the Cowboys.

Christian McCaffrey was particularly troublesome, recording two receiving touchdowns, including a spectacular 66-yard reception late in the contest. Deebo Samuel also contributed a devastating 70-yard rushing touchdown, exposing Dallas' difficulties containing explosive offensive plays.

The defensive problems extend well beyond one disappointing performance. Through 10 games, Dallas has allowed 393.8 yards per contest, the highest average in the NFL.

The Cowboys have also struggled against the run, surrendering 154.1 rushing yards per game, while opponents have converted 48.8% of their third-down opportunities. They're also allowing 28.2 points per game.

These struggles follow an equally difficult 2025 campaign, when the defense surrendered a franchise-record 511 points under former coordinator Matt Eberflus .

Head coach Brian Schottenheimer didn't hide his frustration following the San Francisco defeat, describing the tackling as “atrocious” and the second-half performance as “unacceptable.”

"I thought the second half was unacceptable," he said. "Tackling was atrocious. And we got to do a deep dive on the film and see why. "You can't give up three explosive plays of over 65 yards for touchdowns and expect to win in this league."

One potential solution involves transferring defensive play-calling responsibilities to senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine , who brings considerably more experience in coordinating NFL defenses.

Pettine was brought in to support Parker , making him a possible alternative if Dallas decides to change its approach.

Parker remains in place, but Jones ' willingness to discuss adjustments represents a noticeable shift in tone.

articles.title: The influx of 49ers fans in Dallas didn't surprise Jerry Jones, and he has an explanation: “The most expensive tickets in the NFL”
articles.standfirst: San Francisco supporters made their presence felt at AT&T Stadium during the 49ers' impressive victory over the Cowboys
articles.summary: San Francisco supporters made their presence felt at AT&T Stadium during the 49ers' impressive victory over the Cowboys
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers have enjoyed plenty of success on the road during the 2026 NFL season , but their latest visit to Arlington demonstrated just how far their supporters are willing to travel to watch their team as what should have been a home advantage for the Dallas Cowboys instead featured a sea of red jerseys. It was something that even caught the attention of quarterback Dak Prescott and owner Jerry Jones as San Francisco entered Week 10 with an 8-1 record after defeating Dallas 46-40, extending its best start to a season since 2019, with the 49ers ' supporters were particularly buoyant inside the AT&T Stadium .

Creating an atmosphere that made the Cowboys ' home fixture feel considerably less familiar, and Jones even acknowledged the difference between the visiting supporters had been more noticeable than the home crowd. "Well I don’t know if you saw the price of those tickets that they were paying,” Jones said to 103.5 The Fan. “But it was unbelievable. I would say the highest price of any tickets. Now, I don’t know this, but I would put it up there with the highest price of any tickets that have been sold in the NFL this year. “You add that to the fact that San Francisco has always had a way above average attendance to our away games here in Dallas. You add all that together, that was not a shocker. The facts are, with the way we have the secondary market in tickets today of many of our fans out there as a matter of fact, almost the entire stadium has seat licenses. “They technically own those seats. And so, they’re for the most part, fans that have been out there for years and years and years. A lot of times, our ticket holders will maybe take two or three key games a year and will sell those tickets."

Prescott shocked as 49ers fans took over AT&T Stadium

The atmosphere was only one part of an eventful afternoon as Prescott threw five touchdown passes, with George Pickens recording three touchdowns and 145 receiving yards, as the Cowboys fought back from a 19-point deficit - however, San Francisco 's offence proved too difficult to contain. Accumulating 584 total yards and scoring 29 second-half points, the team managed to win by six points thanks to Christian McCaffrey 's 66-yard touchdown reception ultimately ended Dallas ' comeback hopes, leaving the Cowboys with a 4-6 record in the NFC East . The 49ers continued their impressive campaign, with their travelling supporters providing another reminder of the scale of the franchise's nationwide following and speaking about having to use a silent count inside his own stadium, Prescott admitted he was surprised by the visiting fans. “I told myself early on that the red was for my high school. All I asked for is a great environment to play this game. And unfortunately, their fans were more present than ours,” Prescott said as the team now aims to regroup and go again.

articles.title: Who is Mike Pettine, the senior assistant who will take charge of Dallas Cowboys defense?
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys are finally making a change on the defensive side of the ball after a historically bad start to the season.
articles.summary: The Cowboys are finally making a change on the defensive side of the ball after a historically bad start to the season.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys have finally made a major change to try to save their season. After beginning the year with a 4-6 record, owner Jerry Jones and head coach Brian Schottenheimer had seen enough of a historically bad defense. Jones himself admitted a change could be on the horizon, and it came on Wednesday.

Defensive coordinator Christian Parker isn't going anywhere just yet. He remains the DC, but his playcalling duties have now been taken away. Assuming the mantle of defensive playcaller will be Mike Pettine , who joined the team in October as a senior defensive assistant . Pettine wasn't able to make an impact since joining, but he will now have the best chance to change that.

Mike Pettine has been a defensive coordinator for three NFL teams, and head coach for one other

Pettine is a very familiar name in NFL circles. He rose through the NFL ranks as a key defensive coach in a few roles while with the Baltimore Ravens from 2002 to 2008. He then spent four seasons as defensive coordinator of the New York Jets , then one as the DC of the Buffalo Bills .

After leading strong defensive units, Pettine parlayed that success into his first head coach job, with the Cleveland Browns in 2014. Despite starting his debut season 7-4, he then went 3-18 over his final 21 games. That led to his firing at the end of the 2015 season.

Since then, Pettine has worked as a consultant for the Seattle Seahawks , defensive coordinator for the Green Bay Packers , senior defensive assistant for the Chicago Bears , and assistant head coach for the Minnesota Vikings .

After the 2025 season, Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell announced that Pettine was retiring from coaching. But he got the itch once again when the Cowboys came calling, and he will now be able to put his defensive expertise to full use on gamedays for Dallas.

articles.title: Cowboys’ George Pickens future in doubt as Dallas faces major cap decisions
articles.standfirst: Dallas must decide if George Pickens is worth a blockbuster contract while a defensive overhaul becomes the team’s top priority.
articles.summary: Dallas must decide if George Pickens is worth a blockbuster contract while a defensive overhaul becomes the team’s top priority.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys are still keeping their Playoff hopes alive, but the 2026 NFL season has been filled with challenges that have tested the organization from every angle.

The situation reached a new low this week when Dallas decided to remove Christian Parker from his role as defensive coordinator, a move that could be just the beginning of a major overhaul for a unit that has become one of the team’s biggest disappointments.

Amid the uncertainty, the Cowboys have a clear priority: protecting the few defensive pieces who still represent a foundation for the future. That group is led by defensive tackle Quinnen Williams and cornerback Joey Porter Jr. , who was acquired last month in a trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers.

The biggest obstacle is financial. Dallas already has a significant portion of its salary cap committed to stars like Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb , both of whom are among the highest-paid players at their positions.

That is why securing Porter Jr. long term could become one of the team’s top priorities during the offseason, regardless of who ultimately leads the defense in 2027 . And that decision could have a direct impact on the future of wide receiver George Pickens .

articles.title: Former Cowboys player speaks out after Jerry Jones' latest decision: “This is nasty work, it was all a part of the plan”
articles.standfirst: Dallas handed Mike Pettine responsibility for calling defensive plays, leaving Christian Parker's position under threat
articles.summary: Dallas handed Mike Pettine responsibility for calling defensive plays, leaving Christian Parker's position under threat
articles.body:
Jerry Jones has taken another decisive step in attempting to rescue the Dallas Cowboys ' struggling defense, but the decision to remove play-calling responsibilities from Christian Parker has prompted an angry response from former wide receiver Jesse Holley .

Rather than dismissing Parker following another disappointing defensive performance, Dallas has handed control of its defensive play-calling to senior assistant Mike Pettine , leaving the 34-year-old coordinator in a position that Holley believes could become increasingly difficult.

The change followed Sunday's 46-40 defeat against the San Francisco 49ers, who accumulated 584 yards and scored three touchdowns covering at least 66 yards, exposing weaknesses that have troubled Dallas throughout the season.

However, Holley 's concerns extend beyond the results. Speaking on the DLLS Cowboys podcast, he questioned how players could maintain confidence in a coordinator whose most important responsibility had been handed to someone else.

"This is nasty work. This is some very, very disgusting, despicable, deplorable, filthy work," Holley said.

"If I’m a player in that locker room, who do I trust? Who do I answer to? Do I answer to Mike Pettine? Will he be the DC next year, or won’t he?"

Parker was appointed in January after developing a strong reputation with the Philadelphia Eagles , becoming the youngest defensive coordinator in Cowboys franchise history.

His first opportunity to lead an NFL defense has proved challenging, although Dallas has maintained that his removal from play-calling duties does not represent a complete change in leadership.

Holley nevertheless believes the decision could seriously undermine Parker's authority and complicate his relationship with the players.

"History says, when you lose your play-calling duties, especially the defensive coordinator in the middle of the season, you lose your job at the end of it," Holley explained.

The former receiver also raised questions about Pettine 's appointment in October, suggesting the veteran assistant's arrival may have created an opportunity for Dallas to make precisely this change.

"It feels very snakish," Holley added. "It feels like this was all a part of the plan when they brought Mike Pettine back. They just needed a reason to do it. I don’t like this at all."

Brian Schottenheimer defends Christian Parker

Head coach Brian Schottenheimer has attempted to reassure supporters that Parker remains central to the team's defensive plans despite losing responsibility for calling plays.

"Christian Parker is still our defensive coordinator," Schottenheimer insisted. "He’s a critical piece of what we’re trying to do as we search for answers and solutions. I think he has an incredibly bright future, not just this year, but beyond with us."

Pettine 's history with Parker adds another dimension to the situation, having given the coach his first NFL opportunity with the Green Bay Packers in 2019.

The veteran assistant will take charge of defensive play-calling against the Tennessee Titans on November 22, providing Dallas with an immediate opportunity to evaluate the adjustment.

While Schottenheimer maintains that Parker has a future with the franchise, Holley 's criticism reflects the difficult questions created by separating a coordinator's title from his authority.

articles.title: After canceling her wedding to Dak Prescott, Sarah Jane Ramos reveals what she wants for her future
articles.standfirst: The former fiancée of the Dallas Cowboys quarterback answered a question from her followers about the possibility of becoming a mother again, and her message did not go unnoticed.
articles.summary: The former fiancée of the Dallas Cowboys quarterback answered a question from her followers about the possibility of becoming a mother again, and her message did not go unnoticed.
articles.body:
Sarah Jane Ramos once again drew attention on social media by sharing one of her wishes for the future. After calling off her wedding to Dak Prescott and ending their engagement, the mother of two girls revealed that she is still considering the possibility of having more children.

The statement came during a question-and-answer session on her Instagram stories. A follower wanted to know whether she would like to be a mother again, and Ramos replied with a resounding "Yes!"

Sarah Jane Ramos' response about motherhood

To accompany her reply, Ramos posted a photograph with Aurora, her youngest daughter. Over the image appeared the question "Do you want to have more children?", followed by her statement.

Her response sparked curiosity about the context of her personal life. Ramos and Prescott have two daughters together: Margaret Jane, known as MJ, born in February 2024, and Aurora, who was born in May 2025.

The revelation comes after one of the most talked-about chapters in the personal life of the Dallas Cowboys quarterback. Prescott and Ramos got engaged in October 2024 and were set to marry on April 10, 2026, in Lake Como, Italy. However, the ceremony was canceled weeks before the scheduled date, and the two ended their relationship.

Since then, the two have moved forward with raising their daughters. In April, they reached a temporary agreement on custody and parental responsibilities. Months later, in August, Prescott spoke publicly about the separation and emphasized his commitment to remaining present in the girls' lives.

How many more children does Sarah Jane Ramos want to have?

It is not the first time Ramos has spoken about her desire to expand the family. In October 2025, when she was still engaged to Prescott, she shared during another question-and-answer session that the two of them were considering having two or three more children.

This time, however, she did not specify how many children she would like to have, nor did she make any reference to a future partner. Her answer was brief, but enough to make it clear that she does not rule out experiencing motherhood again.

articles.title: Cowboys WR CeeDee Lamb fires back after bizarre NFL fine
articles.standfirst: CeeDee Lamb had a message for the NFL after a controversial fine left him frustrated following Dallas’ loss to San Francisco.
articles.summary: CeeDee Lamb had a message for the NFL after a controversial fine left him frustrated following Dallas’ loss to San Francisco.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys stayed competitive with the San Francisco 49ers until the gap became clear in Week 10 , falling 46-40 in a high-scoring shootout. The loss was already painful, but the controversy intensified after CeeDee Lamb was fined $30,000 for a hit he delivered on a 49ers defender — while the helmet-to-helmet contact he absorbed drew no penalty at all.

CeeDee Lamb questions the NFL’s standards

Speaking to reporters, Lamb was asked about the league’s decision and made no effort to hide his frustration with the double standard.

“I guess as a receiver, we can get hit, but can’t deliver the punishment,” Lamb said.

Pressed on how frustrating it was to be fined for his own action while the hit he took carried no consequences, Lamb paused, smiled, and delivered a sharp reply:

“Let me punch you and [let me know] how that feels,” Lamb said.

The NFL has tightened its protocols in recent years to protect players, particularly on plays involving head contact. Cases like Lamb’s, however, have reignited the debate over whether every action is being judged by the same standard.

Dak Prescott acknowledges the Cowboys’ difficult reality

Lamb wasn’t the only member of the organization expressing frustration after the defeat. Quarterback Dak Prescott also admitted the team is far from the expectations it carried into the season.

“It’s frustrating for everybody,” Prescott said via ESPN’s Todd Archer . “We didn’t come in with these expectations that we had, obviously thinking that we were going to be dealing with something like this whether it was offense or defense. And it’s part of it. To me, once again, and I know I’ve said it before, the parity of the NFL just shows you how tough it is that you just can’t pick and replace or pick and plug whatever it is and things are just going to automatically get better.”

Sitting at 4-6 , the Cowboys still have a path to stay in the division race, but the margin for error is shrinking fast. The team needs answers quickly if it wants to keep a season full of high expectations from turning into a major disappointment.

articles.standfirst: The Cowboys quarterback opened up about the team’s frustrating 4-6 start and why fixing their problems won’t be as simple as making changes.
articles.summary: The Cowboys quarterback opened up about the team’s frustrating 4-6 start and why fixing their problems won’t be as simple as making changes.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys are navigating another season full of questions. They’re not a complete disaster, but they also haven’t become the dominant team many expected. Sitting at 4-6 , Dallas still has a realistic shot at the NFC East , yet their performance remains well short of the level projected before the year began.

Cowboys defense makes history for the wrong reasons

One of the players most surprised by how the season has unfolded is Dak Prescott. The quarterback acknowledged the frustration inside the locker room but stressed that the team still has time to turn things around.

“It’s frustrating for everybody,” Prescott said via ESPN’s Todd Archer . “We didn’t come in with these expectations that we had, obviously thinking that we were going to be dealing with something like this whether it was offense or defense. And it’s part of it. To me, once again, and I know I’ve said it before, the parity of the NFL just shows you how tough it is that you just can’t pick and replace or pick and plug whatever it is and things are just going to automatically get better.”

Prescott said his priority remains controlling what he can:

“So for me, it’s about making sure that I’m handling my own and continuing doing that. The moment I think that I start looking elsewhere and doing that, you’re not going to get me playing my best ball. All I can do is control what I can.”

The defense became the primary target of criticism after Week 10 , when Christian McCaffrey dominated in the loss to the San Francisco 49ers .

Dallas responded quickly. Days after the game, the team stripped Christian Parker of play-calling duties and handed them to Mike Pettine , though Parker will remain the defensive coordinator. For now, there is still uncertainty about exactly what role Parker will play within the defensive structure in the coming weeks.

While the offense has shown it can move the ball and put up points, the biggest challenge for Dallas is finding answers on the other side of the ball. Without a defense capable of delivering key stops, the Cowboys risk wasting their offensive potential and drifting out of the division race.

articles.title: Is Dak Prescott cursed? His ex, Sarah Jane Ramos, claims to be “the Etsy witch” behind the Cowboys’ bad luck
articles.standfirst: After Dallas’s defense surrendered 46 points in another frustrating home loss, the quarterback’s former fiancée playfully leaned into supernatural fan theories during an Instagram Q&A
articles.summary: After Dallas’s defense surrendered 46 points in another frustrating home loss, the quarterback’s former fiancée playfully leaned into supernatural fan theories during an Instagram Q&A
articles.body:
Watching the Dallas Cowboys stumble to a 4-6 record through the first 10 weeks of the 2026 NFL season has left fans searching for answers, and some are starting to wonder if something supernatural is at work.

Despite boasting one of football’s most explosive offenses behind franchise quarterback Dak Prescott , Dallas has repeatedly been undone by a porous defense.

That imbalance reached a boiling point last Sunday at AT&T Stadium, where the Cowboys fell 46-40 to the San Francisco 49ers after allowing 46 points and 584 total yards, dropping their home record to a dismal 1-4.

With frustration mounting around Arlington, one supporter decided to investigate whether Prescott’s turbulent personal year had spilled onto the turf.

Earlier in 2026, Prescott and his then-fiancée, Sarah Jane Ramos , called off their engagement in March, just one month before their planned April 10 destination wedding in Italy, after Ramos accused the quarterback of infidelity.

Although their romantic relationship ended, the former couple has maintained a steady co-parenting dynamic while raising their two young daughters, MJ and Aurora.

Still, when Ramos opened her Instagram Stories to follower questions on Wednesday night, one user couldn’t resist connecting Dallas’s on-field misfortune to the breakup.

“Did you hire an Etsy witch on Dak”? the follower asked.

Rather than dodging the rumor, Ramos leaned directly into the joke. “This is so silly! I’m the Etsy witch,” Ramos responded.

The term “Etsy witch” refers to independent sellers on the online marketplace Etsy who advertise spiritual and occult-themed “witch” services, ranging from tarot readings and manifestation rituals to hexes and curses, a niche trend that frequently goes viral whenever sports fans look for scapegoats.

Whether Ramos was simply having a laugh at internet gossip or playfully teasing her ex, her sarcastic confession immediately caught fire across social media.

Dak Prescott’s elite numbers prove the curse is only haunting Dallas’s defense

If Ramos actually attempted to cast a spell on Prescott , the hex clearly missed its intended target. Individually, the 11th-year signal-caller is enjoying one of the sharpest statistical campaigns of his career.

Through 10 appearances in 2026, Prescott has completed 64.1 percent of his throws for 2,724 yards, the third-highest passing total in the league, while tossing 21 touchdowns against only six interceptions.

Against San Francisco alone, Prescott threw for 343 yards and five touchdowns on 30-of-51 passing, orchestrating a furious 21-point fourth-quarter rally that nearly erased a 19-point deficit.

Dallas’s downfall had nothing to do with quarterback play and everything to do with a defensive unit that surrendered 9.4 yards per play, letting 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy rack up 389 passing yards and three scores while running back Christian McCaffrey exploded for 223 scrimmage yards and three touchdowns.

Under head coach Brian Schottenheimer , the Cowboys ’ inability to get stops has forced the front office and coaching staff into midseason adjustments, with Schottenheimer announcing defensive changes on Wednesday ahead of Week 11.

Dallas will try to turn its season around when it hosts the 1-8 Tennessee Titans at AT&T Stadium on Sunday, November 22, at 6:00 p.m. GMT. For Prescott and the Cowboys, breaking their supposed bad luck won’t require an antidote from an online marketplace, just a defense capable of holding a lead.

articles.title: Dak Prescott and the Cowboys get one final chance to keep their playoff hopes intact
articles.standfirst: It seems that the only way for them to make the playoffs is to win their division against the Giants
articles.summary: It seems that the only way for them to make the playoffs is to win their division against the Giants
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys entered the 2026 NFL season determined to snap their two-year playoff drought by maximizing the prime years of franchise quarterback Dak Prescott alongside explosive wide receivers CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens . Yet more than halfway through the schedule, a disappointing 4-6 record reflects the exact same defensive collapses that derailed the previous two campaigns.

Following Sunday’s chaotic 46-40 shootout loss to the San Francisco 49ers , in which Dallas surrendered a franchise-worst 584 total yards at home , ownership stripped first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker of play-calling duties, handing the headset to senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine .

Ranking dead last in total defense ( 393.8 yards allowed per game ) and 30th in scoring defense (28.2 points per game) , Dallas has permitted 20 or more points in every single contest this fall.

That relentless leakage forces Prescott, who has thrown for 2,724 yards and 21 touchdowns across 10 games, to operate at an error-free, MVP standard every Sunday just to give his team a fighting chance, an unsustainable formula in the NFL.

Crucial Home Games Offer the Cowboys One Last Lifeline in the NFC East

The lone silver lining in Arlington is that the NFC East remains surprisingly wide open. Division-leading New York Giants (5-3-1) would likely hold a much safer cushion if starting quarterback Jaxon Dart was healthy, leaving the door cracked open for both Dallas and the Washington Commanders (3-5-1) .

For the Cowboys, the next two weeks at AT&T Stadium represent their final realistic chance to keep their playoff hopes alive before heading into their Week 14 bye . Dallas hosts a pair of struggling clubs at the bottom of the league standings: first welcoming the one-win Tennessee Titans this Sunday before facing the two-win Philadelphia Eagles on Thanksgiving Day .

While dropping one of these two home matchups wouldn’t mathematically eliminate Dallas, especially with the Giants facing a tough three-game stretch that includes the Jacksonville Jaguars and San Francisco 49ers , it would effectively put one foot in the postseason grave, as winning the division remains the Cowboys’ only realistic path to January football.

articles.title: Cowboys legend Jimmy Johnson discovers his restaurant in GTA 6 and capitalizes on it by immediately launching some merchandise
articles.standfirst: Hours after Rockstar Games released “Grand Theft Auto VI,” the Pro Football Hall of Fame coach spotted a satirical parody of his Key Largo waterfront restaurant in the game and dropped a custom T-shirt line
articles.summary: Hours after Rockstar Games released “Grand Theft Auto VI,” the Pro Football Hall of Fame coach spotted a satirical parody of his Key Largo waterfront restaurant in the game and dropped a custom T-shirt line
articles.body:
Following more than eight years of anticipation, Rockstar Games officially launched Grand Theft Auto VI on Thursday, November 19, transporting players into the sun-drenched, Vice City-anchored state of Leonida.

Almost immediately, eagle-eyed gamers began spotting satirical nods to real-world South Florida landmarks, including a virtual doppelgänger of Jimmy Johnson ’ s Big Chill, the beachfront dining and entertainment complex owned by the Pro Football Hall of Fame coach in Key Largo.

Rather than simply enjoying the surprise Easter egg from afar, the legendary football coach wasted no time turning the viral gaming moment into an entrepreneurial win.

On Thursday, Johnson shared a screenshot on X and Instagram showing a character stepping inside the fictionalized venue, known in-game as “Tiki Touchdown,” alongside a promotional photo of limited-edition GTA VI-inspired apparel available through his official online store.

“Jimmy Johnson’s Big Chill featured in GTA..shirts at https://jjswagger.com,” Johnson wrote on X.

The featured black half-sleeve T-shirt reimagines the Grand Theft Auto series’ iconic multi-panel cover art through a South Florida lens.

Instead of weapons, fast cars, and heist crews, the retro comic-book grid frames the words “The Big Chill Key Largo” in classic GTA lettering surrounded by illustrations of Johnson wearing sunglasses, a boat, a motorcycle, a frozen drink, a palm tree, and a sunset pier, celebrating both the restaurant’s cameo and Florida’s coastal lifestyle.

How Rockstar reimagined Key Largo’s Big Chill and added other NFL nods

Players encounter the spoofed establishment early in the story campaign during missions set in the Leonida Keys, Rockstar’s fictionalized version of the Florida Keys.

Community map analysts comparing the layout of Key Lento, the in-game counterpart to Key Largo, with trailer footage and launch-day screenshots confirmed that “Tiki Touchdown” mirrors the footprint of Johnson’s real-world waterfront complex.

Even the signage gives the inspiration away: whereas the authentic Big Chill logo displays a vertical football flanked by palm trees and a fish beneath the restaurant’s name, Rockstar’s emblem features a horizontal football paired with a beer glass and palm trees, while adding a classic Grand Theft Auto twist by reimagining the sports bar and grill as a nude bar.

For Johnson, the Key Largo property represents the centerpiece of a second career built around his longtime love of South Florida boating and fishing.

Before opening Big Chill in 2008, Johnson assembled one of football’s most accomplished coaching résumés after beginning his career at Louisiana Tech in 1965.

He won a college football national championship at the University of Miami, built a Dallas Cowboys dynasty with back-to-back Super Bowl championships following the 1992 and 1993 seasons, and guided the Miami Dolphins to three playoff appearances in four years before retiring after the 1999 campaign with an 89-68-0 regular-season NFL record, later earning Pro Football Hall of Fame induction and becoming a staple analyst on Fox NFL Sunday.

While GTA VI marks the franchise’s first foray into the Florida Keys, Johnson’s restaurant is far from the only gridiron reference woven into Leonida.

Vice City’s local football team, the Vice City Manatees, serves as an unmistakable parody of the Miami Dolphins , complete with an airport advertisement depicting a helmet-wearing manatee in slightly altered aqua-and-orange colors.

Elsewhere in an early cutscene, protagonist Lucia wears a black-and-silver No. 15 football jersey modeled after Miami native and Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza, underscoring just how deeply football culture is embedded across Rockstar’s newest open world.

articles.title: Brian Schottenheimer admits the Cowboys could lose a key defensive piece
articles.standfirst: Dallas' defensive shake-up raises fresh questions about Parker's future after Troy Aikman voices concerns
articles.summary: Dallas' defensive shake-up raises fresh questions about Parker's future after Troy Aikman voices concerns
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer has made it clear that Christian Parker's future in Dallas isn't guaranteed after the defensive coordinator lost his play-calling responsibilities.

Although Schottenheimer insists Parker remains important to the team's plans, their recent discussions suggest the situation could have longer-term consequences.

Parker was visibly disappointed after the Cowboys handed defensive play-calling duties to senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine . The 34-year-old admitted he'd challenged the decision and described losing control of the defense as a significant disappointment.

"Not an ideal situation for me personally, but it's what's best for the team at this current point," Parker said.

"So that's how we're moving forward. Continuing to prepare and operate in the same way that we've been doing during the week to have the goal of winning on Sunday."

He also left questions about his future unanswered, telling reporters, "We'll cross that bridge when we get there."

Speaking on 105.3 The Fan's Shan & RJ show on Friday, Schottenheimer revealed that he and Parker had several difficult but productive conversations.

“I don’t think that we missed anything. The big thing is this, guys: every situation is different,” he said.

“Christian’s got a bright future. He’s the defense coordinator of our football team. When you talk about what a defense coordinator does, just one of the parts of being a coordinator is calling plays on defense, and again, I just felt like we needed a different perspective when it came to that.”

Schottenheimer also rejected suggestions that Dallas had misjudged Parker during the hiring process. He explained that calling defensive plays was only one responsibility attached to the coordinator position and that he believed the team needed another perspective.

Troy Aikman questions Cowboys' decision

The coaching change hasn't convinced everyone that Dallas has addressed its underlying problems. Cowboys legend Troy Aikman believes Parker could be taking the blame for difficulties that existed before his arrival.

Speaking to The Dallas Morning News, Aikman questioned why Parker would retain the defensive coordinator title if Pettine was handling the play-calling.

"The Cowboys are desperate. I think [Brian] Schottenheimer's desperate as well with all of the criticism that has come, but I don't know about keeping the title of defensive coordinator if in fact he's not calling the plays," he said.

"I don't know what exactly that that resolves. But there's no doubt that that something needed to happen."

The numbers explain why Schottenheimer felt compelled to intervene. Dallas entered the week with a 4-6 record after surrendering 46 points and 584 yards in its defeat against the San Francisco 49ers. The defense has also ranked last in the league in total and rushing yards allowed, creating mounting pressure on the coaching staff.

Pettine now faces the challenge of improving those performances, beginning against Tennessee. Interestingly, he previously gave Parker his first NFL coaching opportunity in 2019, making their new arrangement an unusual reversal of roles.

Pettine returned from retirement in October and has described his involvement as answering the call from someone who needed help.

Meanwhile, Schottenheimer hasn't committed to Pettine's long-term future in Dallas or confirmed whether he'll remain in the press box while Parker works from the sideline.

articles.title: Who is Mario Narro? The fan who died at age 36 following the brutal Cowboys-49ers brawl
articles.standfirst: A lifelong Dallas Cowboys supporter and New Mexico business owner, the 36-year-old suffered fatal internal injuries during an altercation around kickoff at AT&T Stadium
articles.summary: A lifelong Dallas Cowboys supporter and New Mexico business owner, the 36-year-old suffered fatal internal injuries during an altercation around kickoff at AT&T Stadium
articles.body:
Authorities in North Texas are investigating the death of Mario Narro , a 36-year-old New Mexico resident who died in the hospital three days after falling during a confrontation with another spectator at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas.

Narro had traveled from out of state to watch his beloved Dallas Cowboys take on the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday, November 15, an outing that ended in tragedy for his family and raised fresh alarm over escalating violence at NFL venues.

Outside the stadium, Narro was remembered by relatives as a hardworking entrepreneur and devoted family member.

According to his niece, Claudia DeLara , Narro owned a business in New Mexico and worked in quality control within the food manufacturing industry, often putting in grueling shifts before taking time off to travel and attend major sporting events.

A lifelong Cowboys fan who had previously attended three or four games, he was unmarried, had no children, and maintained a close bond with his parents and extended relatives. Family members also noted that he regularly donated to charities supporting children battling cancer and insisted he was never someone who sought out trouble.

“He was not an angry person,” DeLara told CBS News Texas. “He was not an aggressive person. He was just a jokester.”

According to the Arlington Police Department and accounts shared by Narro’s family, the fatal chain of events unfolded around kickoff on November 15 when Narro fell during an altercation with another fan, an incident relatives say occurred after he was shoved on the stairs between sections 442 and 443.

Remarkably, Narro initially brushed off the impact and remained inside the stadium to watch the entirety of San Francisco ’s 46-40 shootout victory over Dallas.

It was only after the final whistle that Narro began telling friends he was in severe pain. As reported by WFAA, a friend accompanying him flagged down emergency medical personnel at AT&T Stadium, who arranged an ambulance transport to Medical City Arlington Hospital.

Relatives told local media that Narro had sustained severe blunt trauma to his abdomen, resulting in extensive internal bleeding and damage to his intestines and liver that required emergency surgery.

His family contacted Arlington police on Tuesday, November 17, to file an official report, and officers were notified on Wednesday morning, November 18, that he had succumbed to his injuries.

Ongoing police investigation and a troubling wave of stadium violence

Arlington detectives are treating the case as a death investigation and are currently reviewing stadium surveillance footage while awaiting official autopsy findings from the Tarrant County Medical Examiner’s Office to establish the exact cause and manner of death.

As of Saturday, police have not publicly identified the other individual involved in the altercation or announced any arrests or criminal charges.

Speaking on local sports radio station 105.3 The Fan, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones stated that team officials initially had no record of the incident despite the venue’s extensive camera network, adding that the organization is looking into the matter and will cooperate fully with investigators.

Narro’s death occurred against a backdrop of widespread spectator misconduct surrounding the Cowboys-49ers matchup.

Following San Francisco’s win, several unrelated videos surfaced on social media showing brawls between rival supporters, including a heated clash outside AT&T Stadium that required two police officers to break up and another clip capturing a female 49ers fan shoving a Cowboys supporter.

Police noted that roughly a dozen people were ejected during the game, though there is no indication that any of the footage circulating online depicts the confrontation involving Narro.

The unrest in Arlington also echoed similar disorder from the previous weekend, when the 49ers hosted the Las Vegas Raiders in Santa Clara, California.

According to The Independent, police at Levi’s Stadium arrested 11 people, four on suspicion of fighting in public and seven cited for disorderly conduct, while ejecting 45 spectators.

For Narro’s relatives, who drove from New Mexico to Texas only to arrive after he had already passed away, the focus now rests on bringing his body home and uncovering what happened in the stands.

“I think we all agree, we’re just living in a nightmare right now, and we’re hoping we’ll wake up soon,” DeLara said. “It would be nice to have answers, to know what really happened, but that is not what is going to bring him back.”

articles.title: Inconsistency from Dak Prescott is frustrating Cowboys legends
articles.standfirst: Michael Irvin wants greater consistency from Dallas
articles.summary: Michael Irvin wants greater consistency from Dallas
articles.body:
Dak Prescott delivered one of his most impressive performances of the season against the San Francisco 49ers , yet the Dallas Cowboys still came away with another defeat, leaving franchise legends questioning why the offense cannot consistently produce its best football.

Prescott threw five touchdown passes and accumulated 343 passing yards during Dallas' 46-40 loss, but those numbers ultimately counted for little after the defense surrendered 584 total yards to San Francisco.

The result exposed a familiar problem for the Cowboys , as the offense has enough talent to challenge established contenders, but inconsistent execution and defensive shortcomings continue to undermine their chances of winning.

Former Dallas receiver Michael Irvin believes the frustration extends beyond another defeat, questioning why Prescott and his teammates cannot reproduce that level of production more regularly.

"It is pressure to score every time it goes on the field," Irvin said on The Dan Patrick Show. "You put up 40 points on the San Francisco 49ers, you think you got a shot at winning that football game, and we don't win that football game. So that's the sad part about it."

Why Cowboys offense cannot maintain best form

Irvin acknowledged the impressive display against San Francisco but suggested that Dallas would be in a stronger position if similar performances had arrived earlier in the campaign.

"Why can't that offense play like that all the time so we wouldn't be in this situation?" Irvin asked. "If you're gonna put 40 points on San Francisco, why can't you put 40 points on the Giants? You know, that's the thing that we have to figure out."

The Cowboys rank fifth in the NFL with 28.6 points per game and eighth in total offense, averaging 368.3 yards. However, their defense ranks last in yards allowed, surrendering 393.8 per contest, while allowing an average of 28.2 points.

Former Cowboys quarterback Troy Aikman has also questioned the team's offensive approach, suggesting Dallas needs greater balance rather than relying so heavily on its passing attack.

Meanwhile, receiver CeeDee Lamb has expressed his own frustration over the offense's tendency to undermine promising possessions through mistakes.

"We stop ourselves. That sh*t is frustrating. It's annoying. I hate it," Lamb told reporters earlier in November. "Then ultimately we end up losing, so there's that."

Does Dak Prescott deserve more sympathy?

While Irvin believes greater consistency is necessary, former NFL running back LeSean McCoy has argued that Prescott receives too much protection from criticism.

Speaking on Up & Adams, McCoy rejected suggestions that the Cowboys quarterback is continually let down by his supporting cast.

"Dak Prescott will have, he gets a million excuses, right? And if I die, I hope to come back like him," McCoy said.

McCoy pointed to Dallas' previous playoff defeats against San Francisco, arguing that Prescott failed to deliver when the team possessed a more competitive roster.

"There was a point in time where the window was open, and he didn't deliver when they needed him to," McCoy added.

Prescott 's latest performance illustrates the complicated debate in Dallas. He produced five touchdowns against San Francisco, but the Cowboys still lost, demonstrating that quarterback production alone cannot overcome every defensive weakness.

With Tennessee next on the schedule, Dallas has another opportunity to establish consistency before its season slips further away.

articles.title: More trouble for Jerry Jones? Eagles legend predicts 'big upset' when Titans face the Cowboys
articles.standfirst: Defensive weaknesses have convinced LeSean McCoy to back Tennessee
articles.summary: Defensive weaknesses have convinced LeSean McCoy to back Tennessee
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys are facing a game they can scarcely afford to lose, yet former Philadelphia Eagles star LeSean McCoy believes Jerry Jones could be heading for another humiliating result when the Tennessee Titans visit AT&T Stadium on Sunday.

Dallas enters the Week 11 contest with a 4-6 record and an 8.5-point advantage in the betting market, reflecting the considerable difference between the Cowboys and a Tennessee team that has won just once this season.

However, McCoy sees an opportunity for the Titans to exploit a struggling Dallas defense, particularly after the Cowboys surrendered 46 points during their latest defeat against the San Francisco 49ers .

Appearing on Up & Adams with Kay Adams, the former running back was asked to identify his biggest potential upset of the weekend.

"Big upset. I'm going with Titans. The Titans will beat the Cowboys," McCoy declared.

His prediction places additional attention on a Dallas team already under pressure to rescue its season, with Jones overseeing another defensive coaching change following the latest setback.

articles.title: DaRon Bland, at risk of leaving the Cowboys: his injury history complicates his future in Dallas
articles.standfirst: The cornerback will miss the next four games, and his availability for next season is in doubt.
articles.summary: The cornerback will miss the next four games, and his availability for next season is in doubt.
articles.body:
DaRon Bland was placed on the Dallas Cowboys' injured reserve list and will be out of action for at least the next four games. The decision comes after the ankle injury he suffered in the 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers and raises questions about his future with the franchise.

Insider Ed Werder noted that the team’s limited options for bringing players back from injured reserve and the terms of his contract could influence a possible departure .

The concern is not limited to his recovery. Insider Ed Werder warned that Dallas has very few opportunities available to bring players back from injured reserve, so it is not guaranteed that the cornerback will be able to return this season. In addition, his contract situation would allow the team to consider moving on from him next offseason.

Doubts about his return and his future in Dallas

"DaRon Bland will miss the Cowboys' next four games, and there is speculation about whether he will return, considering the team has very few options to bring players back from injured reserve", Werder wrote on X . The journalist also pointed to the conditions of his contract as a factor that could facilitate a possible release during the upcoming offseason.

The defensive back's injury history is another element that raises concern. "He has played 7, 12, and 10 games over the last three seasons due to injuries", Werder added. The lack of continuity has become a problem for a player who once became one of the main anchors of Dallas' secondary.

Bland suffered the most recent injury during the game against San Francisco, played in Week 10 of the season. The move to the injured list means he will miss at least four games. His first chance to return would be in Week 16, when the Cowboys face the Jacksonville Jaguars on December 27.

Dallas also has problems managing its injured players

Bland's situation comes at a complicated time for the roster. According to information published by EssentiallySports, the Cowboys had already used seven of their eight opportunities to activate players who are on the injured list. That limitation reduces their room to maneuver to recover personnel during the final stretch of the campaign.

To cover his absence, Dallas turned to Derion Kendrick , whom they elevated from the practice squad for the game against Tennessee. The move is part of the adjustments the team needs to make in a secondary affected by several absences.

The case also has an economic dimension. Bland signed a contract extension with the Cowboys in 2025, but injuries and difficulties staying available could lead the franchise to reconsider his future. For now, there is no official announcement from Dallas about a possible release: that possibility is part of the speculation raised by Werder.

Bland was selected by Dallas in the fifth round of the 2022 Draft and had his best season in 2023, when he recorded nine interceptions, five of them returned for touchdowns, an NFL record.

That campaign allowed him to earn All-Pro and Pro Bowl honors. Now, his priority will be to recover from the ankle injury, while his contractual future remains subject to the decisions the franchise makes at the end of the season.

articles.title: Contradictory accounts are emerging as Jerry Jones breaks his silence on the death of a fan following the Cowboys-49ers game
articles.standfirst: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones claimed on Friday that the franchise had no record of an altercation at AT&T Stadium
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones claimed on Friday that the franchise had no record of an altercation at AT&T Stadium
articles.body:
Nearly a week after a lifelong Dallas Cowboys supporter suffered fatal internal injuries during a game in Arlington, Texas, team owner and general manager Jerry Jones publicly addressed the tragedy for the first time, and immediately raised new questions about what happened inside AT&T Stadium.

Appearing on Dallas radio station 105.3 The Fan on Friday, the 84-year-old executive suggested he had only just been briefed on the death of 36-year-old Mario Narro and maintained that stadium personnel had no documentation of any physical confrontation.

“I just got that information, and so we had no record of an incident, and we’ll be obviously looking into that,” the 84-year-old said.

“My understanding is that the individual went to the game and didn’t feel good at the game, and then left, and [had] been hospitalized. But we weren’t aware of any incident that involved a fan at the game.”

Jones’s characterization of a fan simply feeling unwell and departing the venue on his own stands in stark contradiction to details released by both the Arlington Police Department and Narro’s relatives.

Even so, Jones defended the security infrastructure inside the 80,000-seat facility, emphasizing that stadium surveillance technology has advanced dramatically over the past 10 to 15 years and monitors virtually every corner of the building on game day.

With roughly 6,000 employees working during a home contest, Jones argued it would be highly unusual for a serious disturbance to unfold without staff noticing, while pledging that the organization will cooperate fully and turn over relevant surveillance video to investigators.

That discrepancy has already drawn scrutiny from legal and sports commentators. Writing for Pro Football Talk, analyst Mike Florio noted that the investigation could carry significant civil liability for the stadium depending on what evidence surfaces, urging law enforcement to use subpoena power to obtain all existing recordings rather than relying solely on footage the franchise voluntarily provides.

What Mario Narro’s family and Arlington police say happened inside AT&T Stadium

For Narro’s loved ones, the timeline of Sunday, November 15, tells a far more harrowing story. A business owner who worked in food manufacturing quality control in Albuquerque, New Mexico, Narro had traveled to Texas to cheer on his favorite NFL team and excitedly sent his father a “Game time!” video from inside AT&T Stadium before kickoff of Dallas’s 46–40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers.

According to Arlington police, Narro fell during an altercation with another spectator around kickoff, an incident his family alleges occurred when a 49ers fan shoved him down a flight of stairs.

Believing at first that he could shake off the impact, Narro returned to his seat for the rest of the matchup, though friends sitting nearby soon realized he was in serious distress.

“He did watch the whole game,” his niece Claudia DeLara told CBS News Texas. “He ordered food. Some drinks. He didn’t touch any of it the whole game. And that’s what tipped off his friend.”

When companions pressed him to show where he had been hurt, the severity of his trauma became unmistakable.

“He did have injuries to his abdomen, where he was bleeding internally,” DeLara said. “You could visibly see on the outside, a bulge of blood and bruising by the end of the game, when they finally took him in.”

Once the game ended, a friend flagged down stadium paramedics, who arranged an ambulance transport to Medical City Arlington.

Admitted to the intensive care unit with severe internal bleeding and damage to his intestines and liver, Narro underwent multiple emergency surgeries before doctors pronounced him dead on Wednesday, November 18, at approximately 11:30 a.m.—one day after relatives filed a formal report with Arlington police on Tuesday, November 17.

As Arlington detectives review stadium cameras and await official autopsy findings from the Tarrant County Medical Examiner’s Office to establish the cause and manner of death, Narro’s family is left mourning a generous, outgoing relative whose passion for live sports brought him to Texas.

“He loved traveling. He loved trying new foods. He loved big events like Cowboys games, UFC fights, boxing,” DeLara told CBS News Texas. “He just really enjoyed being out, being social, being around people, making new friends.”

About a dozen family members drove from New Mexico after learning of his critical condition, arriving too late to say goodbye in person and launching a GoFundMe campaign titled “Bringing Mario Home to Rest” to help cover funeral and transportation expenses.

“For that to be the last time he was alive, it’s like he was so happy to be there, but it is a little bit of a bittersweet feeling,” DeLara said.

“Because that’s also the last time that he was alive.” Looking ahead as investigators seek answers, she added, “We’re just living in a nightmare right now, and we’re hoping that we’ll wake up soon,” DeLara told CBS News Texas.

articles.title: CeeDee Lamb leaves Michael Irvin behind in Cowboys franchise history
articles.standfirst: CeeDee Lamb etched his name into Cowboys history with a record-breaking performance against the Titans.
articles.summary: CeeDee Lamb etched his name into Cowboys history with a record-breaking performance against the Titans.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys returned home this Sunday to face one of the weakest teams of the season in the Tennessee Titans . After the questions raised by their narrow win over the Indianapolis Colts last week, Dallas answered with authority and quickly seized control of the game, heading into halftime with a comfortable 27-9 lead.

CeeDee Lamb continues to make history in Dallas

The clear star of the first half was CeeDee Lamb , who once again showed why he is regarded as one of the most important receivers in recent franchise history. The Cowboys star recorded nine receptions for 103 yards and a touchdown before the break, a performance that also allowed him to set a new team record.

“CeeDee Lamb has recorded 1,000+ receiving yards in six consecutive seasons, the longest streak in Cowboys history. He broke the tie with Hall of Famer Michael Irvin (five),” NFL Research posted on X.

With this achievement, Lamb continues to build his legacy in Dallas and adds another argument for those who rank him among the greatest receivers ever to wear the star. Even Michael Irvin has publicly endorsed his career and allowed him to wear the historic No. 88 that defined Irvin’s own legacy.

The Cowboys needed a convincing performance after laboring more than expected against the Colts, and this time they wasted no opportunity to dictate terms from the opening whistle. Still, the team will need to sustain that intensity through the second half.

Under head coach Brian Schottenheimer , Dallas has struggled at times to manage large leads, so preventing another opponent comeback will be a top priority regardless of the scoreline.

After this matchup, the next challenge for CeeDee Lamb and the Cowboys is a highly anticipated home game against the Philadelphia Eagles on Thanksgiving Day .

articles.title: Dak Prescott brings Jerry Jones joy and immediately sends a message following the Cowboys' latest victory
articles.standfirst: Dak Prescott praised the Cowboys' offensive line after Dallas' dominant win over the Titans, sending a confident message ahead of a crucial Thanksgiving showdown with the Eagles.
articles.summary: Dak Prescott praised the Cowboys' offensive line after Dallas' dominant win over the Titans, sending a confident message ahead of a crucial Thanksgiving showdown with the Eagles.
articles.body:
D ak Prescott delivered a confident message after the Dallas Cowboys ' dominant 51-30 victory over the Tennessee Titans, a result that keeps the team's NFC playoff hopes alive.

The quarterback turned in one of his best performances of the season, completing 28 of 33 passes for 325 yards and four touchdowns , while adding nine rushing yards and another score on four carries.

Following the game, Prescott spoke with Fox and made sure to credit the offensive line, calling their performance the biggest reason behind Dallas' explosive offensive showing.

"I'll start with the offensive line. You look at those stats right there, and I see that many yards passing, and I don't think I had a sack. It's credit to the guys up front giving us time, giving us opportunities, and just the pass catchers going out there doing their thing. And we're just consistently talking all game long that we got an opportunity to score. Let's go do it, and I think we did on every possession. That's the standard of this offense," Prescott said.

The Cowboys quarterback also emphasized the mindset the team carried throughout the game.

"We talked all game long about taking advantage of every opportunity to score. We went out and did it. I think we scored on just about every possession. That's the standard we want for this offense," he added.

Cowboys' offense sends a statement

Dallas needed a convincing performance to stay in the NFC playoff race , and it answered with an offensive showcase from start to finish.

The Cowboys built a commanding 27-9 halftime lead and never lost control, even as the Titans mounted a modest rally in the second half.

Running back Javonte Williams helped balance the offense with 18 carries for 67 yards and a touchdown , while also catching three passes for 24 yards and another score.

Meanwhile, KaVontae Turpin made the most of his limited opportunities, turning two carries into 41 yards and a touchdown .

Through the air, CeeDee Lamb was once again Prescott's favorite target, hauling in 11 receptions for 132 yards and a touchdown . George Pickens also topped the 100-yard mark with seven catches for 102 yards and another score , while Brevyn Spann-Ford added two receptions for five yards and a touchdown.

Next up is a major test for Dallas. The Cowboys will host the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 12 on Thanksgiving Day , a matchup that could play a pivotal role in shaping their season.

articles.title: Embarrassing image for Jerry Jones: a viral photo shows the Cowboys fan boycott in action
articles.standfirst: Even a 51-30 blowout win over the Tennessee Titans could not erase the sting of a viral pregame snapshot showing thousands of unfilled seats inside AT&T Stadium
articles.summary: Even a 51-30 blowout win over the Tennessee Titans could not erase the sting of a viral pregame snapshot showing thousands of unfilled seats inside AT&T Stadium
articles.body:
On the field Sunday afternoon in Arlington, Texas, the Dallas Cowboys delivered their sharpest offensive showcase of the 2026 NFL season, dismantling the visiting Tennessee Titans 51-30 behind five total touchdowns from Dak Prescott and a record-breaking 132-yard receiving performance from CeeDee Lamb .

Yet before Dallas improved to 5-6 on the year and dropped Tennessee to 1-9, the most talked-about moment of the day had already unfolded in the stands, and it painted an uncomfortable picture for owner and general manager Jerry Jones .

Entering the Week 11 FOX broadcast with a disappointing 4-6 record, the Cowboys faced a steep drop in local enthusiasm against a one-win Titans squad.

Roughly a quarter-hour before kickoff, FOX 4 Dallas sports anchor Jeff Kolb posted a photograph from inside AT&T Stadium revealing sweeping sections of empty blue seats across the lower and upper bowls of the 80,000-seat venue.

“Lots of empty seats at Jerry World 15 minutes before kickoff against the Titans,” Jeff Kolb shared on X.

For a franchise that routinely leads the NFL in announced attendance and prides itself on turning every home date into a prime-time spectacle, the sight of wide-open rows just before the opening whistle struck a nerve.

Although additional spectators filtered in after kickoff, the viral image immediately became fuel for critics who argue that three decades without a Super Bowl appearance, combined with soaring game-day costs, have finally pushed loyal supporters to their breaking point.

Why longtime Cowboys supporters are calling for a boycott of Jerry Jones

Sunday’s sluggish pregame turnout followed weeks of escalating anger across Cowboys Nation.

Throughout the fall, frustrated fans on social media have openly called for a “boycott” of home games until Jones relinquishes control over football operations.

That frustration boiled over one week earlier when visiting San Francisco 49ers fans visibly took over AT&T Stadium during Dallas’s 46-40 loss, prompting a longtime season ticket holder to publish a blistering viral critique aimed directly at the 84-year-old owner.

“I was absolutely sickened yesterday watching that Dallas Cowboy game. Let me set the stage. I’ve been a Dallas Cowboy fan since I was a little girl. I remember watching Staubach, Dorsett, & Randy White when Dallas was America’s Team. When I moved to Dallas, I immediately bought season tickets. I’ve had them for going on 25 years. Jerry Jones has absolutely, unequivocally ruined the franchise. The downfall started when he fired Jimmy Johnson . Then he decided to move from Irving to Arlington to create his Mega Stadium resulting in all season ticket holders having to pay again for their seat licenses at astronomical rates,” one fan began.

“My seat was about 20 rows up on the 50 yard line Irving & now I’m on level 3 at about the five yard line and I still had to pay about twice what I paid for my 1st two seat licenses in Irving. And you raised ticket prices through the roof to about $350 a seat for the lower bowl starting price. Jones , you priced-out the amazing blue collar, hard-working Dallas fans. They can’t afford a seat much less parking that is between $200 and $250 a game.

“All you see is Corporate America in the seats now because only corporations and the rich can afford to go. So Jerry , when you look at the Dallas Cowboys Stadium fans and see wall-to-wall 49ers fans with a spattering of blue jerseys, this is why.

“When Dallas makes a great play and you hear Boos, this is why. When opposing teams make a great play and the crowd erupts, this is why. Jerry, all you have done is ruin a franchise both on and off the field for the sake of lining your pockets. The Cowboys will Never be Americas Team until you are gone.”

Whether Sunday’s empty seats stemmed from an organized protest, steep resale and parking prices, or simple apathy toward a sub-.500 matchup, the message sent to ownership was unmistakable.

Even with Dallas rebounding on the scoreboard against Tennessee ahead of Thursday’s high-profile Thanksgiving Day showdown against the rival Philadelphia Eagles , winning back the trust of disillusioned hometown fans will take far more than a single Sunday blowout.
