articles.title: Alarm bells in Dallas? Dak Prescott sporting mysterious bandage on his hand days before Cowboys' Thanksgiving showdown against the Eagles
articles.standfirst: Cowboys receive unexpected Dak Prescott injury scare just days before crucial Eagles showdown
articles.summary: Cowboys receive unexpected Dak Prescott injury scare just days before crucial Eagles showdown
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys finally have momentum on their side after weeks of inconsistent results, but their preparations for Thanksgiving have been complicated by an unexpected injury scare involving quarterback Dak Prescott .

Dallas produced one of its most convincing performances of the season on Sunday, defeating the Tennessee Titans 51-30 at AT&T Stadium to improve to 5-6 and maintain hopes of recovering from its disappointing start.

However, attention quickly shifted away from the result when Prescott appeared at his postgame press conference with a bandage wrapped around his left hand.

With the Philadelphia Eagles visiting Dallas on Thursday, the sight immediately raised questions about whether the quarterback had sustained an injury that could affect his preparation for the divisional matchup.

Prescott moved quickly to reassure supporters, explaining that the bandage was a precaution following a heavy collision during the game.

"It's good," Prescott told reporters when questioned about his hand. "Just on that nasty hit or whatever. I mean, if that's the worst that came from it, I'm super, super thankful. They just got bent back a little bit. I'm fine."

Prescott plays down hand injury

The encouraging update came after Prescott delivered another impressive offensive display, completing 28 of 33 passes for 325 yards and four touchdowns without an interception.

He also avoided being sacked throughout the contest, helping Dallas repeatedly exploit Tennessee's defense during a dominant afternoon.

The quarterback has now thrown nine touchdown passes across his previous two games, establishing a Cowboys franchise record for the most passing touchdowns over a two-game span.

Although his latest injury involves his non-throwing hand, Dallas will still be mindful of the limited recovery time before facing Philadelphia.

Prescott previously encountered a similar concern earlier this season when his throwing hand required treatment after a defender stepped on it during a victory over the Houston Texans.

On that occasion, the quarterback dismissed fears of a significant injury, insisting there was no lasting problem with his hand.

The Cowboys will hope his latest reassurance proves equally accurate, particularly given the importance of Thursday's matchup.

Cowboys face additional injury worries

Prescott wasn't the only Dallas player requiring medical attention against Tennessee, with linebacker Dee Winters suffering a right knee contusion during the second quarter.

Winters was injured while attempting to tackle former Cowboys running back Tony Pollard and required assistance leaving the field, leading to uncertainty over his availability for Thanksgiving.

Cornerback Cobie Durant also underwent evaluation following an accidental collision with teammate DeMarvion Overshown during a fourth-quarter tackle.

Head coach Brian Schottenheimer subsequently confirmed that Durant had been cleared to return, although Dallas decided against risking him with the result already effectively settled.

Philadelphia also enters the contest with injury concerns after cornerback Quinyon Mitchell suffered a hamstring injury during Sunday's 19-16 victory over Pittsburgh.

The Eagles have strengthened their pass rush in recent weeks, recording 10 sacks across their past two games, creating another challenge for Prescott and the Dallas offense.

With Thursday's contest scheduled for 4:30 p.m. ET, both teams face a compressed recovery period ahead of another important NFC East meeting.

articles.title: Dak Prescott and the Cowboys make NFL history against the Titans with a never-before-seen feat
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys have made scorigami in their last two games
articles.summary: The Cowboys have made scorigami in their last two games
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys kept their flickering 2026 NFL season alive on Sunday, though they will need to be nearly flawless the rest of the way since winning the NFC East over the New York Giants (6-3-1) and Washington Commanders (3-5-1) remains their only realistic path to avoiding a third straight year without playoff football.

Improving to 5-6 after a dominant 51-30 victory over the Tennessee Titans , franchise quarterback Dak Prescott put on an absolute clinic at AT&T Stadium, completing 28 of 33 passes for 325 passing yards, four passing touchdowns, and a rushing score .

Wideouts George Pickens (seven catches, 102 yards, one touchdown) and CeeDee Lamb (11 receptions, 132 yards, one touchdown) both eclipsed the century mark while finding the end zone, with Lamb surpassing 1,000 receiving yards for a franchise-record sixth consecutive season in the process.

Back-to-Back NFL Scorigamis Highlight Dallas Cowboys’ High-Scoring Identity

Beyond the blowout win itself, Sunday’s 51-30 final score officially went into the record books as an NFL Scorigami , marking the 1,101st unique final score in league history and the first time any pro game has ever ended with that exact tally.

Remarkably, it came just seven days after Dallas’ 46-40 shootout loss to the San Francisco 49ers also registered as a Scorigami , meaning the Cowboys have now produced two never-before-seen final scores in consecutive weekends.

That bizarre historical quirk stems directly from a glaring imbalance on the roster: because a leaky defense continues to surrender points in bunches, Prescott and the offense are forced to score at a relentless pace just to stay competitive.

Underscoring that dynamic, Dallas became just the second team in NFL history to score 325 or more points while allowing 310 or more points through its first 11 games of a season, joining the infamous “Greatest Show on Turf” 2000 St. Louis Rams .

With zero margin for error remaining, the Cowboys turn right around to host the Philadelphia Eagles (3-7) on Thanksgiving Day in a must-win divisional clash before plunging into a daunting December gauntlet.

Following the holiday showcase, Dallas hits the road to face wild-card contenders in the Seattle Seahawks prior to its Week 14 bye, then travels west again to battle the Los Angeles Rams .

The Cowboys will close out the regular season by welcoming the Jacksonville Jaguars after Christmas, hosting the Giants in Week 17, and finishing on the road against the Commanders.

articles.standfirst: Dak Prescott’s hand injury sparked concern in Dallas. Brian Schottenheimer finally delivered an update.
articles.summary: Dak Prescott’s hand injury sparked concern in Dallas. Brian Schottenheimer finally delivered an update.
articles.body:
A Dak Prescott injury at this point in the season could be a devastating blow for the Dallas Cowboys , a team that is still trying to find consistency and remain in the fight for an NFL Playoff spot.

The Cowboys responded with authority after a difficult week, crushing the Tennessee Titans 51-30 in NFL Week 11 , a victory that improved their record to 5-6 on the season.

Although the win came against a Tennessee team with just one victory this year, Dallas’ offensive performance provided a much-needed boost of confidence after a week filled with pressure following the decision to remove the defensive coordinator from play-calling duties.

The biggest star once again was Dak Prescott, who delivered another spectacular performance by throwing four touchdown passes and adding one rushing touchdown, recording five total touchdowns for the second straight game. The quarterback also surpassed 300 passing yards for the third consecutive contest.

However, Prescott raised concerns after the game when he arrived at his postgame press conference with his left hand wrapped. The situation created some uncertainty because the Cowboys have a short week before facing the Philadelphia Eagles on Thanksgiving, meaning any physical issue could become a major concern.

The Cowboys quarterback attempted to calm concerns and insisted the issue was not serious.

“It’s good. Just on that nasty hit or whatever. I mean, if that’s the worst that came from it, I’m super, super thankful. They just got bent back a little bit. I’m fine,” he said.

Despite Prescott’s comments, injuries are always handled carefully around the NFL, which shifted attention to head coach Brian Schottenheimer , who addressed the media on Monday .

articles.title: Cowboys legend sets deadline for Jerry Jones to keep America's most prestigious title
articles.standfirst: Michael Irvin explained why Dallas cannot depend on its historic success forever
articles.summary: Michael Irvin explained why Dallas cannot depend on its historic success forever
articles.body:
Three decades without a Super Bowl victory have done remarkably little to diminish the Dallas Cowboys ' national profile, but franchise legend Michael Irvin believes Jerry Jones is approaching a deadline that could determine whether the organization retains its identity as 'America's Team'.

The Hall of Fame receiver, who helped Dallas establish its dominance during the 1990s, fears the franchise's extraordinary popularity cannot always compensate for its failure to compete for championships.

Dallas hasn't appeared in a Super Bowl since defeating the Pittsburgh Steelers 27-17 in January 1996, leaving an entire generation of supporters with no personal memories of the team's greatest achievements.

During an interview with CNBC Sports, Irvin suggested another decade without a championship could fundamentally change how younger football fans perceive the Cowboys .

“You can’t be America’s Team if a whole generation goes by and never experiencing the glory of a championship story from the Dallas Cowboys,” Irvin said.

“A generation is forty years. Considered forty years in the Bible. So you got about 10 more years that you got to make sure over these next few years you get a championship.”

Why Jones can't rely on Cowboys history forever

The prospect of Dallas losing its cultural significance carries particular importance for Irvin , whose three Super Bowl victories helped establish the legacy that continues to underpin the franchise's commercial success.

“All of my work is at stake because if you lessen what the brand is and you take it away from being America’s team, people don’t look in on it now,” Irvin explained.

“Whoever gets to see all of my work and the history and learn the history behind it? So all of us got to stand on each other’s shoulders.”

Nevertheless, Irvin stopped short of holding Jones entirely responsible for the championship drought, highlighting the Cowboys ' three consecutive 12-5 regular seasons between 2021 and 2023.

“Jerry’s put enough talent on that team that they went three years in a row at 12-5 and got in the playoffs,” Irvin said. “Jerry didn’t make any throws. They could have won those games. So you ask, ‘has he done enough?’ I say, ‘yes.’”

Prescott's great form and Dallas' biggest weakness

Irvin 's more immediate concern surrounds a defense that gave up 584 total yards during the Cowboys ' recent 46-40 defeat against the San Francisco 49ers , undermining another outstanding performance from Dak Prescott .

“So yes, something has to happen on defense, and it has to happen now,” Irvin insisted.

Dallas subsequently defeated Tennessee 51-30 to improve to 5-6, with Prescott throwing four touchdown passes and strengthening the Cowboys ' hopes of returning to the postseason.

Head coach Brian Schottenheimer believes the quarterback is enjoying an exceptional period in his career, telling reporters: “I can honestly say, I can’t remember a stretch that he’s played this well. I think he’s in a really good spot right now.”

Yet Prescott 's brilliance alone can't resolve the defensive shortcomings that continue to limit Dallas' championship prospects.

The Cowboys remain a commercial powerhouse, but Irvin believes Jones must eventually deliver something that marketing and nostalgia are unable to provide, which is a championship that belongs to the next generation.

articles.title: Jerry Jones’ $30 million Salvation Army gift sets a campaign record during a Cowboys Thanksgiving tradition
articles.standfirst: The Gene and Jerry Jones Family’s historic gift marks three decades with the Salvation Army and will help expand its work in North Texas
articles.summary: The Gene and Jerry Jones Family’s historic gift marks three decades with the Salvation Army and will help expand its work in North Texas
articles.body:
A Cowboys Thanksgiving tradition now comes with a record-setting gift. The Gene and Jerry Jones Family has donated $30 million to The Salvation Army of North Texas, the largest contribution to its One Army, Many Fronts campaign to date. Announced Tuesday, Nov. 24, the gift supports the organization’s work across the region.

The donation is tied to a new 21-acre Dallas Social Services Campus near Love Field. The project is designed to bring several kinds of help together, including emergency shelter, addiction recovery programs, supportive housing and health services. The Salvation Army says the campus is expected to serve 600 people through its regular programs and up to 900 during severe weather. Its first services are expected to open in 2027.

The gift also marks 30 years of the Jones family’s partnership with the Salvation Army. The Cowboys’ Thanksgiving halftime show first served as a national launch for the Red Kettle campaign in 1997 . Since then, the annual event has helped bring national attention to the charity’s holiday fundraising drive. The Cowboys say the partnership has helped raise more than $3.4 billion for the Salvation Army.

A Cowboys tradition with a local purpose

The anniversary celebration took place Monday at AT&T Stadium, which was lit red for the occasion. Four generations of the Jones family gathered at the event, alongside Cowboys cheerleaders, for photos marking the milestone.

On Thanksgiving , the Cowboys will continue the tradition during halftime of their game against the Philadelphia Eagles, with Miranda Lambert scheduled to perform.

The Salvation Army’s work extends beyond its familiar holiday kettles. Its services include food and shelter, disaster assistance, rehabilitation and youth programs.

The new Dallas campus is part of a broader $212.7 million campaign; the campus project itself accounts for $154.8 million. The $30 million gift is a major contribution to that plan, though the organization has not said it will cover the entire project.

The public announcement connects the gift to the family’s three-decade relationship with the Salvation Army and to a specific North Texas project.

articles.title: The Dallas Cowboys and Jerry Jones Thanksgiving table face a familiar enemy
articles.standfirst: Thanksgiving brings another high-stakes NFC East battle, with an old rival standing in Dallas' way
articles.summary: Thanksgiving brings another high-stakes NFC East battle, with an old rival standing in Dallas' way
articles.body:
Thanksgiving in Dallas comes with high expectations, and this year, the stakes are difficult to ignore. Jerry Jones has another opportunity to see his team make a statement on one of the NFL's biggest regular-season stages. The holiday matchup also arrives at a critical point in the Cowboys' campaign. With the NFC East race still offering a path forward, every game carries added importance as the season approaches its final stretch.

The Philadelphia Eagles return to Dallas with plenty at stake

The Cowboys will welcome the Philadelphia Eagles on Thanksgiving, renewing a divisional rivalry that has already produced a one-sided result this season. Dallas defeated Philadelphia 38-21 in Week 7, giving the home team reason to believe it can repeat that performance.

The Eagles enter the matchup at 3-7, while Dallas holds a 5-6 record and is trying to catch the 6-3-1 New York Giants in the NFC East standings. Philadelphia has also suffered a major setback with Jalen Hurts ruled out for the remainder of the season because of blood clots. J oe Milton III has taken over at quarterback, but his performances have yet to provide much offensive consistency.

Jerry Jones has reasons to expect a strong performance

Dallas comes into Thanksgiving after an impressive 51-30 victory over the Tennessee Titans. The Cowboys have been one of the league's most productive offensive teams, averaging 30.6 points per game and ranking second in red-zone touchdown efficiency. D ak Prescott has also benefited from strong protection, having been sacked on only 3.45% of his dropbacks, the lowest rate in the NFL.

However, the defensive numbers remain a concern for Jones and the Cowboys . Dallas allows 28.4 points per game and ranks last in the league in yards allowed per rushing attempt, as well as third-down defense . Those weaknesses could give Philadelphia opportunities to stay competitive, particularly if Saquon Barkley is healthy enough to contribute despite dealing with neck and illness issues.

The Cowboys enter as favorites in the Thanksgiving showdown

According to James Bryer's Thanksgiving NFL preview for Gridiron Experts, Dallas has a projected 74% chance of winning, with the model forecasting a 31-22 victory . The Cowboys also have an advantage on the ground against a Philadelphia defense that has struggled to stop opposing offenses.

Still, the Eagles have reasons to approach the game with confidence after their previous meeting, even if the circumstances have changed considerably . Dallas opened as a 7.5-point favorite before the line moved to 8.5, reflecting the difference between the teams' current situations. For Jones, another Thanksgiving appearance offers the Cowboys a chance to strengthen their playoff hopes while facing one of their most familiar divisional opponents.

articles.title: Brian Schottenheimer’s Cowboys future hangs in the balance after insider drops major new update in Dallas
articles.standfirst: Brian Schottenheimer’s future in Dallas is under scrutiny as the Cowboys face mounting pressure.
articles.summary: Brian Schottenheimer’s future in Dallas is under scrutiny as the Cowboys face mounting pressure.
articles.body:
Brian Schottenheimer arrived in Dallas with high expectations, but his tenure as Cowboys head coach could already be in jeopardy. In his first season he finished 7-9-1 and missed the playoffs, and the outlook in his second year does not look much brighter.

The Cowboys are coming off a dominant 51-30 win over the Tennessee Titans —the first game after Schottenheimer stripped defensive coordinator Christian Parker of play-calling duties. Still, at 5-6 , Dallas needs a strong response to climb back to .500 before their Thanksgiving matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles .

And while the team searches for stability, the pressure on Schottenheimer continues to mount.

Schottenheimer needs the playoffs to keep his job

ESPN reporters Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano listed the Cowboys among the teams that could make a coaching change at the end of the season.

The only other team mentioned was the New Orleans Saints , led by former Dallas offensive coordinator Kellen Moore .

“The vibes out of Dallas leadership are not great,” Fowler reported. “The Christian Parker move was not universally well-received in the building. This might be a case where coach Brian Schottenheimer needs a playoff berth to ensure a third season.”

Graziano agreed, noting that another losing campaign could signal the end of the Schottenheimer era in Dallas.

The Cowboys are more patient with coaches than their reputation would lead you to believe. But they had very high hopes for this season. If it fizzles out because they blew the defensive coordinator hire, and Schottenheimer gets to the end of the year with another losing record, I think there would be some smoke there.

The situation contrasts with the strong public support Schottenheimer received in January, when owner Jerry Jones said the coach was “one of the reasons for our fans to be excited about the future.”

According to The Dallas Morning News , Schottenheimer signed a four-year contract when he was hired in January 2025 .

The Christian Parker situation complicates the picture

Improving the defense was Dallas’s top priority in the offseason. In 2025 , the Cowboys allowed a franchise-record 511 points (30.1 per game) and lost four of their final five contests.

They responded by hiring Christian Parker , the former Eagles pass-game coordinator and defensive backs coach, who became the team’s third defensive coordinator in three years.

The results, however, never arrived.

Dallas currently ranks 28th in the NFL against the pass, and the crisis reached its peak after the team allowed 46 points in a 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Week 10.

Days later, Schottenheimer handed defensive play-calling duties to senior assistant Mike Pettine , who had joined the staff in October . Parker retained the title of defensive coordinator but with a reduced role.

According to DLLS , Parker even considered resigning after losing those responsibilities. Still, Jerry Jones publicly defended him, saying the experience could help him grow as a coach.

articles.title: Why Aaron Rodgers' criticism of Mike McCarthy rings painfully familiar to Dallas Cowboys fans
articles.standfirst: The quarterback has reopened an uncomfortable chapter in with the former head coach
articles.summary: The quarterback has reopened an uncomfortable chapter in with the former head coach
articles.body:
Mike McCarthy 's final seasons with the Dallas Cowboys are back under scrutiny, but the latest questions have come from an unexpected direction as Aaron Rodgers ' dispute prompted a reporter to revisit concerns that, in his view, helped define the coach’s departure. Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram argued that complaints about preparation, game-planning and player relationships were part of McCarthy 's Dallas story as he pointed to the 2023 bye week, when players reportedly confronted the coach after a 42-10 loss to the San Francisco 49ers , and pushed for offensive changes.

McCarthy was in his first season and was calling plays at the time, but Dallas finished that campaign 8-3 before losing heavily to the Green Bay Packers in the playoffs before the Cowboys then went 7-10 in 2024, and his contract was not renewed, closing his five-season tenure. And Rodgers brought Dallas into the conversation on Wednesday, after learning he would be benched for Pittsburgh's Week 12 game and then released as appearing on The Pat McAfee Show, the four-time NFL MVP said he had asked people about McCarthy 's previous teams and heard familiar accounts. "I looked into what was going on in Dallas [when McCarthy was the Cowboys' coach] and what happened there," Rodgers said. "And it's the same thing that went on in Green Bay for a decade because the coaches and the support staff there know exactly what happened."

A familiar story for those who followed McCarthy in Dallas

Harris said the issues Rodgers described would not surprise people who followed McCarthy 's exit from Dallas as he cited alleged indifference toward draft evaluations, poor game-planning and players having to challenge the coach. Harris' remarks are his assessment of McCarthy's Dallas tenure, however, not independent proof of each allegation Rodgers has made about the Steelers boss, but his sharpest criticism concerned preparation this season as he claimed the coach had admitted on several Tuesdays to not watching the previous Sunday's game film. “Multiple times he said that he doesn't watch film when I've talked to him on Tuesdays. He hasn't seen the film yet," Rodgers claimed, as he also alleged McCarthy slept during a meeting that week and ended a Steelers halftime huddle with "one, two, three, Packers." Rodgers said he confronted McCarthy privately on Monday before the conflict became public, as he argued the habits were unhealthy and demanded change, warning, "If you try and bench me or don't change the play call, then you should just release me." The Steelers subsequently released him and that could be the final chapter of his storied career in the NFL , but for now that is also why the latest dispute has landed differently in Dallas as Rodgers ' accusations have reopened a conversation about the McCarthy ’s final Cowboys seasons that never fully went away.

articles.title: Philadelphia Eagles vs Dallas Cowboys: Where to watch the Thanksgiving Day game live and what time it starts
articles.standfirst: Cowboys and Eagles reignite the hottest rivalry in the NFC East on Thanksgiving Day
articles.summary: Cowboys and Eagles reignite the hottest rivalry in the NFC East on Thanksgiving Day
articles.body:
The quintessential divisional rivalry returns, and this time with a turkey involved. The Dallas Cowboys host the Philadelphia Eagles at AT&T Stadium in Arlington as the main event of the traditional Thanksgiving Day celebrations, a matchup no longer for first place in the division, but one that retains all its bite.

Both teams are coming off an inconsistent season , but with different reasons to fight until the last yard.

When and where to watch the Eagles vs Cowboys game?

The NFL Week 12 game between Dallas and Philadelphia is scheduled for this Thursday, November 26, 2026 , at 4:30 pm (3:30 pm Central Time and 1:30 pm Pacific Time), at AT&T Stadium , which has a capacity of 80,000 fans.

In the United States, the national broadcast of this Thanksgiving Day game is on Fox ; while you can follow it via streaming on TUBI and NFL+

Overview of both teams for the Thanksgiving Game

The season's snapshot doesn't favor either team when compared to the elite. In the NFC East , the New York Giants lead the pack with a 6-1-3 record , while Dallas sits in second place with 5 wins and 6 losses , and Philadelphia brings up the rear with 3 wins and 7 losses . In the overall league standings, the Cowboys are in 18th place and the Eagles, mired in 26th.

Dallas' offensive numbers tell a peculiar story: with 337 points for , they are one of the most productive teams in the league, but their 312 points against reveal a defense that bleeds easily.

It's a series of shootouts. Philadelphia is the exact opposite: just 167 points scored , the most lackluster offense between these two, and a -70 point differential that explains why they've lost so much.

The all-out duel between Dallas and Philadelphia: the Week 7 rematch

You don't have to look far to find the immediate precedent. In Round 7 , on October 27, the Cowboys went to Philadelphia and suffered a resounding 38-21 defeat , one of the toughest blows their opponent has taken all season. Dallas will want to repeat the formula; the Eagles are looking for revenge on the road.

Recent form tips the scales in favor of the home team. Dallas is coming off a 51-30 rout of the Tennessee Titans in Round 11, an offensive showcase that confirms their ability to rack up wins when their offense is firing on all cylinders.

In contrast, Philadelphia comes off a 19-16 win against the Pittsburgh Steelers , barely their first victory since Week 2. Before that respite, the Eagles had accumulated a bitter streak that included the aforementioned blowout against the Cowboys themselves and two losses against Washington and the Giants.

On the home side, the attack revolves around quarterback Dak Prescott and a top-level receiving corps led by CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens , with Jake Ferguson as a weapon on the tight end and the running back duo of Javonte Williams and Kendre Miller .

It's an arsenal built to win high-scoring games , just the kind of game Dallas is comfortable in.

Philadelphia relies on its identity of balance and physical dominance. Jalen Hurts leads an offense anchored by star running back Saquon Barkley , with DeVonta Smith as the primary aerial threat and Dallas Goedert at tight end.

The problem, reflected in those 167 points scored , is that the offense hasn't found its rhythm this season. If Hurts and Barkley don't dominate on the floor, the Eagles will have enormous difficulty keeping up with Dallas's offense.

What's at stake heading into the Playoffs

For the Cowboys, this game is a matter of survival in the playoff race . At 5-6 , they're below .500 and need to string together wins to stay alive in the fight for a wild card in the NFC , where the competition is fierce with teams like San Francisco (9-1), Detroit, and Chicago (both 8-2) setting the pace.

Winning a divisional game at home , against a historic rival and in a national showcase like Thanksgiving , would be the perfect morale boost.

For Philadelphia, the situation is much grimmer.

At 3-7 and at the bottom of the NFC East , their season is spiraling downward. The win over Pittsburgh showed there's still pride in the locker room, but mathematically, the margin is narrowing week by week. Another loss to their most hated rival would leave their campaign teetering on the brink.

Cowboys vs Eagles Prediction: Who will win the Thanksgiving Day game?

Everything points to a high-octane game in Arlington . Dallas' offense is firing on all cylinders, and Philadelphia, with its lower production, will have a hard time matching it, and the 38-21 record against them is a significant factor.

If the Cowboys can keep their offense from drying up, logic dictates they'll repeat that feat in front of their home crowd on Thanksgiving Day . Prediction: Dallas Cowboys win in a high-scoring game.

articles.summary: Cowboys collapse in shocking fashion as Brian Schottenheimer faces intense backlash.
articles.body:
It was inevitable that Brian Schottenheimer would face intense criticism after watching what appeared to be a sure victory slip away in the final seconds of the Thanksgiving showdown between the Dallas Cowboys and Philadelphia Eagles .

Jake Elliott delivered a stunning 59-yard field goal with just two seconds remaining to give the Cowboys’ division rival a dramatic 39-38 victory . Cameras immediately turned toward Schottenheimer after the heartbreaking loss, capturing a devastated expression that led many fans online to suggest it was the look of a coach who already knew he could be facing serious consequences.

A completely unexpected ending

The Eagles (4-7) received a shocking opportunity to complete the comeback after Schottenheimer decided to go for it on fourth-and-1 from the Philadelphia 39-yard line with just 55 seconds remaining.

The decision backfired. Dak Prescott was sacked , allowing Philadelphia to regain possession and use its final drive to reach the Dallas 41-yard line with only seven seconds left, setting up Elliott’s game-winning kick.

The crushing defeat will only increase the pressure on Schottenheimer, as the Cowboys (5-7) once again failed to build momentum with consecutive victories and made their path to the playoffs even more difficult.

Dallas controlled much of the matchup, building a 21-point lead in the third quarter and still holding a 14-point advantage in the fourth . However, the Eagles mounted an improbable comeback after blocking a punt and returning it for a touchdown, a play that completely shifted the momentum and sparked Philadelphia’s dramatic turnaround.

articles.title: Cowboys collapse on Thanksgiving, but Jerry Jones isn’t ready to pull the plug on Schottenheimer
articles.standfirst: Jerry Jones makes Brian Schottenheimer decision after Cowboys’ shocking Thanksgiving collapse
articles.summary: Jerry Jones makes Brian Schottenheimer decision after Cowboys’ shocking Thanksgiving collapse
articles.body:
Despite suffering one of the most painful losses in their recent history on Thanksgiving, the Dallas Cowboys have no plans to make drastic changes right now.

After a dramatic 39-38 defeat to their NFC East rival, the Philadelphia Eagles , team owner Jerry Jones made it clear that he is not considering a coaching change and continues to stand behind head coach Brian Schottenheimer .

While defending his head coach, Jones still acknowledged the severity of the loss, calling both the result against Philadelphia and the team’s overall situation this season “devastating.”

The blow was especially hard for Dallas, which dominated much of the game and held a 21-point lead in the third quarter , while still leading by 14 points in the fourth . But the Cowboys completely collapsed down the stretch, allowing 22 points in the final period and letting a game they appeared to have under control slip away.

The decisive sequence came in the final minute. Dallas elected to go for it on fourth-and-1 from the Philadelphia 39-yard line , only for Dak Prescott to be sacked for a nine-yard loss, handing the Eagles a golden opportunity.

Philadelphia capitalized. Quarterback Joe Milton completed a couple of passes for 14 yards, setting up Jake Elliott for a 60-yard field goal in the closing seconds that sealed the stunning comeback.

“It’s a bitter disappointment to have done some things early that we did and turn around…” Jones said of the defeat. “Every phase. Every phase that’s a part of a game like this. All three teams (offense, defense, and special teams), ownership, coaching, everybody is responsible for what we saw at the end of that game.”

Schottenheimer, 53, took over as Cowboys head coach ahead of the 2025 season but failed to lead the team to the playoffs after finishing with a 7-9-1 record .

After Jones publicly reaffirmed his support, Schottenheimer was asked about his job security and made it clear he isn’t concerned about his employment situation.

“I don’t worry about that. I worry about the guys in that locker room. That doesn’t affect me.”

With the loss to Philadelphia, the Cowboys find themselves in a precarious position once again in the playoff race. Dallas sits in third place in the NFC East at 5-7 , with very little margin for error in the final stretch of the season.

articles.standfirst: Following Aaron Rodgers' explosive criticism of Mike McCarthy, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones didn't hesitate to reveal exactly how he feels about his former head coach.
articles.summary: Following Aaron Rodgers' explosive criticism of Mike McCarthy, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones didn't hesitate to reveal exactly how he feels about his former head coach.
articles.body:
Before addressing Brian Schottenheimer's future following the heartbreaking loss to the Philadelphia Eagles , Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones made one thing clear: he wasn't about to let Mike McCarthy take the blame for the criticism coming from Aaron Rodgers .

Jerry Jones breaks silence to defend Mike McCarthy after Aaron Rodgers' accusations

The Cowboys squandered a 14-point fourth-quarter lead and suffered a crushing 39-38 defeat to the Eagles at AT&T Stadium on Thanksgiving after Jake Elliott drilled a game-winning 60-yard field goal .

Despite the devastating collapse, Jones reiterated his full confidence in Schottenheimer as Dallas' head coach. However, he was also asked about the growing controversy between Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy and now-free-agent quarterback Aaron Rodgers .

According to ESPN's Brooke Pryor , the 84-year-old owner had nothing but praise for McCarthy, who coached the Cowboys from 2020 through 2024 before being replaced by Schottenheimer.

"He's frankly one of the finest people around football that I've been around. I never had the type of thing that's being said about him. I never had that in any type of consideration in my time with him extending his contract, any of that. That was never on the table. We never had an issue within the organization," Jones said.

Jones also recalled hiring McCarthy after the veteran coach spent a year away from the NFL following his departure from the Green Bay Packers .

During his five seasons in Dallas, McCarthy compiled a 49-35 record , won two NFC East titles , and guided the Cowboys to four playoff appearances .

Jones' comments come just days after Rodgers blasted McCarthy during an appearance on The Pat McAfee Show , where the four-time NFL MVP claimed the Super Bowl-winning coach would fall asleep on the job . Rodgers was waived by the Steelers on Wednesday.

For Jones, however, the priority remains getting the Cowboys back on track. Sitting at 5-7 , Dallas is running out of time and must respond quickly to keep its playoff hopes alive.

articles.standfirst: Weeks after leaving the Dallas practice squad, Milton orchestrated the biggest comeback in Thanksgiving history
articles.summary: Weeks after leaving the Dallas practice squad, Milton orchestrated the biggest comeback in Thanksgiving history
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys didn't have to look far to identify the quarterback responsible for their Thanksgiving collapse. Joe Milton III , who was still a member of their practice squad last month, orchestrated a remarkable Philadelphia Eagles comeback before delivering a pointed reminder of how well he understood his former team's defensive vulnerabilities.

Milton finished with 331 passing yards and three touchdowns as Philadelphia recovered from a 21-point deficit to claim a dramatic 39-38 victory, completing the largest comeback in NFL Thanksgiving history.

His explanation for finding success against the Cowboys was particularly uncomfortable for an organization that had allowed him to leave only weeks earlier.

“I know that defense like the back of my hand,” Milton said after the victory, according to Fort Worth Star-Telegram reporter Nick Harris.

Milton served as Dak Prescott 's backup last season before losing his position to Sam Howell during the preseason. Philadelphia subsequently signed him from Dallas' practice squad following the injury that ended Jalen Hurts ' season.

Thursday marked only Milton 's third career NFL start, yet the quarterback produced a performance that could have significant consequences for the NFC East playoff race.

Philadelphia appeared to be heading toward another disappointing defeat after Dallas established a 28-10 halftime advantage and extended its lead to 31-10 during the third quarter.

The Eagles were also dealing with injuries to running back Saquon Barkley and cornerback Cooper DeJean , both of whom were forced out during the opening quarter.

However, Milton connected with DeVonta Smith for touchdown receptions of 50 and 45 yards, found Makai Lemon for another score and added a 14-yard rushing touchdown.

Philadelphia accumulated 22 points in the fourth quarter before kicker Jake Elliott converted a 59-yard field goal with two seconds remaining, completing an extraordinary turnaround.

“A lot of emotions, but mainly just so happy for this team,” Milton said. “This team never let up. These guys on the sideline, they never dropped their head. Everybody just kept saying, ‘We’re good, we’re good. We’re gonna keep going.'”

Brian Schottenheimer sends warning to Cowboys

Dallas' defensive problems were well established before Thursday's defeat, with the Cowboys allowing 389.5 yards and 28.4 points per game through their opening 11 fixtures.

Head coach Brian Schottenheimer nevertheless emphasized that responsibility for surrendering such a commanding advantage extended beyond the defensive unit.

“But as I said, we had a chance with the ball in our hand offensively to put the game away, and we didn’t. All three phases had a hand in this one,” Schottenheimer explained.

The Cowboys now sit at 5-7, while Philadelphia has improved to 4-7 following consecutive victories, keeping its divisional ambitions alive.

Losing a game from such a dominant position would have been damaging enough for Dallas. Having its defensive weaknesses exposed by a quarterback who recently occupied a place on its practice squad makes the Thanksgiving defeat considerably harder to digest.

articles.title: Stephen A. Smith mercilessly mocks Cowboys and Dak Prescott after Thanksgiving loss to the Eagles
articles.standfirst: Dallas surrendered a 21-point advantage on Thanksgiving
articles.summary: Dallas surrendered a 21-point advantage on Thanksgiving
articles.body:
Even Stephen A. Smith appeared stunned by the manner in which the Dallas Cowboys managed to lose on Thanksgiving, with the ESPN host struggling to contain his laughter after watching Dak Prescott and his teammates squander a commanding lead against the Philadelphia Eagles .

Dallas suffered a remarkable 39-38 defeat at AT&T Stadium on Thursday, surrendering a 21-point advantage in the largest comeback in NFL Thanksgiving history.

Adding to the embarrassment was the identity of the quarterback responsible for Philadelphia's resurgence as former Cowboys backup Joe Milton III .

Smith had actually backed Dallas to win during Thursday morning's edition of ESPN's First Take, declaring: “There’s no reason on earth that the Cowboys should lose this game.”

By the closing stages, however, the outspoken analyst could scarcely believe what he was witnessing.

“You can’t make this up! I can’t believe that the Dallas Cowboys are even in a position to lose this game. This is unbelievable!” Smith wrote on X as Philadelphia threatened to complete its comeback.

His reaction became even more animated following the final whistle, with Smith sharing a video of himself laughing at the Cowboys ' latest setback.

“A third stringer who used to be on the Cowboys last year comes back from a 31-10 deficit,” Smith said. “You can’t make it up. Look. Oh my God. Just when you think it can’t get worse, they figure out a way.”

Joe Milton delivers Thanksgiving humiliation

Dallas appeared to have victory within its grasp after building a 28-10 halftime lead and subsequently extending its advantage to 31-10. Even midway through the fourth quarter, Prescott 's 14-yard touchdown run had given the Cowboys a seemingly comfortable 38-24 lead.

However, Joe Milton threw for 331 yards and three touchdowns, adding another score on the ground as Philadelphia mounted an extraordinary recovery. The Eagles scored 22 fourth-quarter points, with Jake Elliott converting a 59-yard field goal with two seconds remaining.

Milton 's performance was particularly painful for Dallas given that he had occupied a place on the organization's practice squad until October, before Philadelphia recruited him following Jalen Hurts ' season-ending injury.

Dak Prescott admits costly mistake

Despite completing 19 of 28 passes for 291 yards and two touchdowns, Prescott was left regretting a decisive fourth-and-1 play that ended with Ty Robinson sacking him for a nine-yard loss with 55 seconds remaining.

“That’s one I’ll think about for a long time,” Prescott said. “Still had a chance at the throw, just so the DB was playing CeeDee pretty physical. And then I couldn’t get off of that, felt the pressure, and took the sack. And I can’t do that. Most important part of the game.”

Head coach Brian Schottenheimer defended his decision to attempt the conversion rather than punt: “I wanted the ball in Dak’s hand. I trust our quarterback, our offense.”

Dallas now sits at 5-7, with its postseason probability falling from 19% to 8%, according to Next Gen Stats.

A difficult road game against the Seattle Seahawks awaits, leaving the Cowboys with little margin for further mistakes and Smith with another memorable reason to question their championship credentials.
